clue.text: Left, invariably, with time to make purchase

parts.note: invariably means always, which is ever
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone always takes their time over making a purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying here: it means grip or mechanical advantage, the sense of a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase can mean a firm hold or mechanical advantage, which is exactly what a lever supplies.

clue.text: Poet given short measure

parts.note: low means short in height
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: A versifier is sold short.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Lowell and James Russell Lowell were American poets.

clue.text: Without prompting, divulge one wasn't impressed

definitions.meaning: someone who enlisted freely rather than being forced into service

explanation.surface: Someone lets slip that they were not much taken with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressed' is not 'awed': it means pressed into service, as by a naval press gang.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer information unbidden, or a recruit who signed up of their own free will.

clue.text: Clothes let out, with end taken in

indicators.note: taken in means the piece is put inside another

parts.note: to rent is to let out property
an aim is a goal or end

explanation.surface: Garments are let out and then taken in at the end, as by a tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' and 'taken in' sound like dressmaking; they are rent and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for garments.

clue.text: Impudent child and maiden splitting the profit

indicators.note: splitting means one piece divides the other by going inside it

parts.note: gain means profit
M is the abbreviation for a maiden over in cricket

explanation.surface: A cheeky youngster and a girl share the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored, written M.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a cheeky young scamp.

clue.text: Old country joins others in S. America and Asia, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means each country loses its last letter, keeping most of the word

parts.note: Peru is one of the other countries of South America
Siam, the old name for Thailand, is a country in Asia

explanation.surface: An ancient kingdom is lumped together with nations of South America and Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims both countries: PERU loses its U and SIAM its M, leaving PER + SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia is the former name of Iran, an empire of the ancient world.

clue.text: The new member is a competitive type

definitions.meaning: someone just joining a group or profession
a person who goes in for a contest

explanation.surface: The latest recruit is a pushy sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrant is someone joining an organisation, and also a competitor in a race.

clue.text: Cut tail off the bird

parts.note: to snip is to cut

indicators.note: tail off picks the last letter of the word the

explanation.surface: Someone lops the tail off a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tail off' reads as an instruction to remove a tail, but it gives the tail of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snipe is a wading bird with a long bill.

clue.text: Test players, in a sense

definitions.meaning: a trial performance by actors or musicians

explanation.surface: Trying out performers, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing is the sense of sound, and a hearing for performers is a trial.

clue.text: Doctor died, leading to one mystery

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of the BBC series
a unit is a single thing, one

explanation.surface: A doctor's death sets off a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story about who committed the crime.

clue.text: Bill for a sovereign, preceded by two others

definitions.text: Bill for a sovereign, preceded by two others

parts.words: Bill for a sovereign, preceded by two others
parts.note: Bill is a pet name, so the king it stands for is the one who came after two earlier kings of the same name

explanation.surface: A banknote paying for a gold coin, with two more ahead of it in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' and 'sovereign' look like money (a sovereign is an old British gold coin), but Bill is short for a first name and the sovereign is a king: the third English king of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Orange reigned as the third English king called William, after the Conqueror and Rufus.

clue.text: Light one omitted from internal layout

indicators.note: layout signals the remaining letters are set out in a new arrangement
omitted from says a letter is taken out of the word internal

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A lamp is left out of a building's interior plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Omitted from' removes I from INTERNAL, leaving NTERNAL; 'layout' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, so it gives light.

clue.text: Brewer, for example, briefly retains beer, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: retains means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable is a dictionary, abbreviated DICT
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A man who makes beer holds on to some of it while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: Brewer looks like someone who makes beer, but it is E. Cobham Brewer, author of a famous reference book; DICT holds ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect is a regional variety of a language, a way people talk.

clue.text: To abandon aircraft is not funny

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of is not are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ditching an aeroplane is no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' reads as humorous but rearranges IS NOT into TISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, so to abandon something.

clue.text: Stakes public funds on a bet, we hear

parts.note: stock is government securities, public funds

indicators.note: we hear means a word is given by its sound

parts.note: to abet is to aid, so a bet heard as one word means help

explanation.surface: Someone gambles the public purse on a wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bet' is heard as 'abet', meaning aid, which sounds like ADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive fence made of upright stakes.

clue.text: Rate is just part of the system, politically

indicators.note: just part of says the answer is only a short run of letters inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Speed counts for little in the political machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Rate is just' as the definition, but 'is just' cannot stand in for a noun; 'Rate' is the definition, 'is' links and 'just part of' signals the run sysTEM POlitically.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is pace or speed, as in the rate at which music or events proceed.

clue.text: Suspicion spy chief is yielding to pressure

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
giving means bending or yielding under pressure

explanation.surface: Doubts arise that the intelligence chief is cracking.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension.

clue.text: Standard scores provided with almost all Wagner's work

parts.note: par in golf is the standard score for a hole
if means provided that

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Orchestral scores of nearly everything Wagner wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores' looks musical but means golf scores, pars.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is Richard Wagner's last opera.

clue.text: Absolutely defeated rival for land

definitions.meaning: in Sheridan's play The Rivals, Bob ... is the suitor beaten to Lydia by Captain Jack Absolute
units of land area, measured by the acre

explanation.surface: A competitor utterly beaten for territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absolutely' looks like 'completely' but means 'by Absolute': Captain Absolute and Bob Acres are rivals in The Rivals, an 18th-century English comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute beats the bumbling Acres in Sheridan's comedy; acres also means estates or stretches of ground.

clue.text: Contract for North — South and East briefly involved

indicators.note: involved means twisted together, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A bridge contract bid by North, with South and East briefly in the auction.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge setting misleads: 'involved' mixes NORTH with S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten something is to make it smaller, as muscles contract.

clue.text: Make the most of one's hour outside after work

indicators.note: after means this part follows the piece for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: outside means the word for hour wraps around the other piece

parts.note: an hour is a time
one's gives I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: Someone getting the best out of their free hour once the job is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is the usual crossword op (opus); 'one's' supplies I plus S, which the word for hour wraps around before the work comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To optimise something is to get the best possible result from it.

clue.text: It serves to remind me guide's incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is lost

parts.note: a mentor is a guide

explanation.surface: A reminder that my adviser's work is unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake kept as a reminder of a person or event.

clue.text: Rig up a net for one of the lower seeds

indicators.note: rig means fix or manipulate, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting up a net for a tennis match among the lower seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seeds' suggest tennis rankings; the seed grows underground, so 'lower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A groundnut is a seed that ripens below the soil, hence a low-down seed.

clue.text: County cricket side returned in bad mood

indicators.note: in means the turned piece sits inside the word for bad mood

parts.note: a sulk is a fit of bad temper

indicators.note: returned means the letters of the cricket side are read backwards

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A county cricket team comes home sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns OFF into FFO, placed 'in' SULK. Cricket's off side is the half of the field the batter faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is a county on the east coast of England.

clue.text: Criticize bad service

definitions.meaning: in tennis, a serve landing outside the box

explanation.surface: A complaint about poor service.
explanation.definitionFit: To find blame in something, and a failed serve in tennis.

clue.text: Accumulate in business many a fortune

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
a pile is slang for a large fortune

explanation.surface: Someone builds up a great deal of wealth in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a pile' is British slang for getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To compile is to gather material together, so to amass it.

clue.text: Valley thoroughly searched? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is left off

parts.note: combed means searched thoroughly

explanation.surface: A valley has been scoured, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: A combe is a short valley, a word common in southern English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a short steep valley or hollow in a hillside.

clue.text: Time to find me — in hours, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps means the words before it could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A request to be tracked down within hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges all thirteen letters of 'to find me in hours'.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, time is treated as an extra dimension alongside the three of space.

clue.text: Is such a recital animated at all?

parts.note: lit up means animated or lively
any can mean at all, as in 'is it any good?'

explanation.surface: A dull list of complaints: is there any life in it?
explanation.walkthrough: The question doubles as a joke, since such a recital is famously monotonous.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long repetitive list, as of prayers or grievances, recited aloud.

clue.text: Purchased French art inside, as asked

indicators.note: inside means the French word sits within the other piece

parts.note: bought means purchased
in French tu es means 'thou art', so art is es

explanation.surface: Someone bought French art when asked to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old verb, as in 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Besought is the past of beseech, to beg or plead.
